title: Clearer runtime choices, resilient restarts, and safer Spark displays
summary: CloudlessOS 0.2.7-4 makes recipes the guided default, clarifies active model and recipe controls, improves private API and Tailscale setup, and hardens kiosk, display, engine, update, and automatic-runtime recovery on DGX Spark.
changes: Make Recipes the first and default Model Manager view, separate Recipes and Models into full-width choices, move language and image types into filters, and warn standard-interface users before running an unoptimized standalone model.
Identify the active Desktop runtime as a recipe or model and provide direct actions to open Model Manager, inspect its exact details, or stop it.
Explain vLLM and recipe-selected engines in the standard interface while keeping permanent API identity and advanced engine controls behind Advanced interface.

Keep API Access controls synchronized after API-key creation or deletion, default new keys to Model and agent access, show reachable LAN addresses, and organize client instructions and security activity into collapsible sections.
Clarify Tailscale SSH versus regular SSH over a tailnet, refresh connection state automatically, and expose the exact private HTTPS address created by Tailscale Serve.
Validate the structured tool-calling contract used by the Cloudless Agent so incompatible default runtimes fail visibly instead of producing a misleading lost-engine response.

Normalize single-display ownership, recover safely from phantom or disconnected monitors, and keep the Cloudless kiosk on the intended physical output across hotplug, repair, package update, and reboot.

Restart the kiosk exactly once after a successful appliance update so interface changes appear immediately, while preserving rollback behavior and avoiding desktop disruption in side-by-side DGX installations.

Persist the exact recipe or model that was running before restart, explain manual and automatic recovery choices, and wait for the protected container broker before automatically restoring a recipe after cold boot.

Add a DGX Spark SM121 vLLM runtime build, strengthen managed recipe container startup and recovery, and expand regression coverage for runtime identity, remote access, display topology, update continuity, and restart behavior.
